# Architecture Options

The Awtsmoos can reveal one light through many vessels; Awtsmoos.com must choose the vessel that stays truthful as the project grows.

## Option A — edit every app/game HTML page

High fidelity but high churn. Rejected as the default because dozens of files would duplicate metadata logic and drift from registries.

## Option B — generated wrapper/detail pages

Safe and deterministic, but creates duplicate user-facing URLs and weakens canonical identity. Useful only for pages that cannot accept central enrichment.

## Option C — central static-HTML response enrichment

Inject missing canonical/title/description/robots/H1 metadata from authoritative registries when serving known app/game entry documents. Strongest default if the server exposes a narrow response hook without invasive global behavior.

## Option D — service-worker/client metadata

Rejected for search-critical metadata because crawler visibility must not depend on hydration.

## Option E — sitemap/catalog only

Already implemented; useful discovery, but insufficient when detail pages have weak or missing semantic metadata.

## Selected direction

Prefer Option C if a narrow, testable server hook exists. Fall back to targeted whole-file page rewrites only for a small number of exceptional entrypoints. Translation and alias enrichment remain generator/index-based rather than global middleware.
